page.layout: Printed page 153, one text block with marginal notes in the right margin. Top: running head and page number. Below the head, a quotation from Bellarminus set as an indented block. Centred heading "I. ANIMADVERSIO." with an italic subtitle, a "Sect. II." side note beside it. Then the main paragraphs, with notes in the right margin. Foot: signature "V." and catchword "Nihil".

main_text.l: Viri sancti (vt Vos censetis) prærogatiuam, tanquàm
Typhum (sic enim appellabant) repulerint; quantis, ob-
secro, sannis Bonifacium VIII. excepissent, præ cuius su-
perbia, vel insania potius, Illius Typhus modestia videre-
tur? quùm nimirùm hic supra summos Monarchas,
etiam in Temporalibus, Speculæ suæ fastigium attolleret:
De quo *supra. Tu perge, & Speculationis officium ex-
pone.
Bellarminus de Offic.

main_text.l: I. ANIMADVERSIO.

l.i: Speculandi officium, Episcopis omnibus æquè impositum,

main_text.l: QVid nobis hic Pontifici tuo peculiare occurrit?
quid non etiam cuiuis legitimo Episcopo commu-
ne? hanc enim Speculam aliis Episcopis omnibus com-
munem esse, vel hoc nomen Episcopus, ex communi Eth-
nicorum, nedùm Christianorum, vsu satis ostendit.
I. Apud Ethnicos. {a}Episcopi nomen (ait Balbus) à ve-
tustis temporibus deductum: nam Athenienses quos
speculatum mittebant, quid ni unusquisque Subditorum civitate
boni maluè ageretur, Eos Episcopos, id est, Speculatores vocabant;
ut apud Plutarchum Scipio Africanus Episcopus gentium; &
Cicero ad Atticum Episcopus in oris maritimis dicebatur.
Nec multò aliter {b}Onuphrius. Atque hanc Specula-
tionem ex Alto faciendam esse, plurimae in Scripturis
metaphoræ denotant. Vox enim prædicantis Alta esse
debet; {c}Iohannes erat vox clamantis: Exemplum eius
in Alto; {d}Lucerna non sub modio, sed in candelabro posita:
Locus in Alto, nimirùm, in celeberrimo hominum con-
centu; {e}Quicquid didicisti in aure prædicate super tectum.

marginalia.note: Onuphr. Tract. de obscur. vocum Ecclef.[?] interp.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "sannis" (Bonifacium passage) and "nedùm" (accent as printed) are uncertain. "Ecclef.[?]" in the note b is hard to read; it may be "Eccles." The reference marks a, b, c, d, e and * are small superscript letters and were placed where they stand in the text. The italic runs are estimated from the scan, especially the stretch from "tustis" to "dicebatur". The "Sect. II." side note has been attached to the subtitle heading, as it stands beside it in the margin. The quotation's opening and closing marks are as printed.
